assessment: Reported practice and preparation fall below targets among returned slips, but 72 slips cover 97 attendances and speaking time was not measured. Attendance continuity, pairing delays and task confusion suggest testable possibilities, not established causes. Both proposals are hypotheses requiring six-session outcome and workload checks.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: give each partner different information about a fresh, self-contained everyday scenario so even a newcomer has something their partner needs to learn.
openings.delta: Preserve the familiar session structure while replacing shared conversational history with reciprocal information gaps. Offer optional sentence starters without proficiency labels; use four six-minute exchanges with alternating lead roles and one optional partner change.
openings.prediction: Occasional attendees report easier entry and more useful practice; speaking becomes less concentrated within pairs. Allocated lead time alone does not establish useful speaking time.
openings.probe: Compare matched shared-sheet and split-information rounds, reversing order across sessions. Anonymously observe actual speech distribution; collect usefulness and entry-difficulty reports with optional recent-attendance counts. Track preparation and printing time against the weekly cap.
assumptions: Reusable split-information sheets can be prepared within unpaid volunteer capacity.
Information asymmetry stimulates conversation at differing levels without becoming a reading exercise.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: use one enduring preparation mission: bring one real question you want to ask in the language. Learner questions become the next session's conversational material.
openings.delta: Replace changing topic-dependent homework with a stable, meaningful action printed on every sheet and available on paper at the venue. Anyone arriving unprepared can choose a question from existing prompts, preserving access after absences.
openings.prediction: Earlier-task errors and preparation clarification messages decline while prepared questions generate useful conversation. Topic-selection effort decreases sufficiently to offset question support.
openings.probe: Across six sessions, ask every attendee to name the next preparation action without viewing the sheet; record whether brought questions actually support useful speaking. Log coordination activities separately and audit paper access for absent participants. Assess the original 80%, 85% and under-90-minute targets.
assumptions: The venue permits dependable paper pickup between sessions.
A repeated mission remains useful across levels and does not narrow conversational variety.
